transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-07-09 16:00 PDT; Duration: 48m; Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Derek Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (SageWorks Head of Growth), Omar Haddad (Events Manager), Lena Park (Demand Gen)

Summary: Quick sync to align the global roadshow content, ABM lead-gen plays for EMEA and NA, speaker logistics, and campaign timeline. Discussed session formats (talk + demo vs panel), demand-gen funnel, and measurement/KPIs. Agreed on next steps and owners.

Topics: 1) Session formats and run-of-show 2) Target accounts and regional priorities 3) Content collateral and speaker logistics 4) Campaign channels and timeline 5) VE/AV and technical dry-run

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll go about 45 minutes. Quick, um, agenda — run of show, speakers, lead-gen motion.
[00:25] Priya Singh: Yeah hi, thanks. We're trying to lock the London and Austin stops, want to make sure the content appeals to both platform teams and product managers, not only the ML folks.
[00:40] Derek Chen: Totally. From an SE perspective we can craft a 12 minute demo that shows latency/cost comparisons and the rollout story; keep it non-ops heavy but have slides in appendix.
[01:05] Omar Haddad: Quick logistics — London venue is a 150 person theater, AV has HDMI + DisplayPort, no on-site NDI, streaming via local encoders. Need confirmation if you need a wired LAN.
[01:28] Lena Park: For promo, we're planning account-based ads + partner co-mailers; also want to test a gated whitepaper vs ungated registration to pump signups.
[01:45] Priya Singh: Our primary KPI is MQLs from target account list and SQLs created within 30 days, secondary is demo requests.
[02:10] Ava Martinez: Regarding format options — panel vs single speaker + demo. For target audience product folks might prefer a panel with customer seats, while infra people want deeper demo. Thoughts?
[02:34] Derek Chen: Suggest hybrid: 25 min high-level panel, then 12 min focused demo breakouts. Or breakouts in the afternoon so the main session stays product-focused.
[03:02] Omar Haddad: Logistically, that adds complexity for AV and rooming, but manageable if we have two adjacent rooms.
[03:25] Priya Singh: Budget note — we have limited sponsor slots. Redwood could do a co-branded breakout table and a 10 minute demo slot if we help with travel stacking.
[03:48] Ava Martinez: Yep happy to explore sponsorship model. We'll propose two tiers: demo slot + lead share, or shared panel only.
[04:05] Lena Park: For the email nurture — we'll run three touches: save-the-date, one week reminder, and day of. Wanna test subject lines: 'How to cut inference costs' vs 'Make LLM inference 10x cheaper' — one is softer, one is more provocative.
[04:32] Derek Chen: Note — be cautious about '10x' claims unless we have benchmark backing. We can provide conservative numbers in the deck.
[04:50] Priya Singh: Also need speaker bios — can Redwood provide concise 2-3 sentence blurbs and headshots?
[05:05] Ava Martinez: Yes, will send. Also attaching a quick 'demo two-minute' script for the presenter to keep things tight.
[05:22] Omar Haddad: AV question — do you plan to run live inference from the cloud? If so, we need low-latency fallback for demos.
[05:40] Derek Chen: We'll run on dedicated capacity for the live demo with a local cache fallback — that reduces risk. We'll include failover notes in the dry-run checklist.
[06:02] Priya Singh: On demand-gen targeting, we'll share top 200 accounts for EMEA and top 300 for NA; need your list of compatible ICP filters.
[06:20] Ava Martinez: We'll map ICP to our audience segments and share a nurture playbook.
[06:35] Lena Park: Question on tracking — can Redwood provide UTMs for landing pages and a webhook for lead ingestion into our CRM?
[06:49] Derek Chen: Yes, we have tracking templates and can provide a webhook. We'll confirm payload fields; some names may be slightly different in our system.
[07:05] Priya Singh: Competitors — our ops team looked at GiantCloud AI and CloudPrompt running similar roadshows; want to differentiate on reliability and cost transparency.
[07:25] Ava Martinez: Good point, we'll emphasize SLOs and cost controls in the deck.
[07:37] Omar Haddad: One more — do you have AV run of show templates? If Redwood can share a venue-ready script that would save us time.
[07:50] Ava Martinez: We'll share a detailed run of show and checklists – including mic cues, slide advancer, demo lead SOP.
[08:05] Priya Singh: Timeline check — launch campaign start date target is 2025-08-01, events in late September.
[08:20] Derek Chen: That should give us 3–4 weeks to finalize decks and dry runs.
[08:35] Ava Martinez: Ok, let's summarize the commitments and owners.
[08:45] Priya Singh: Also, I think we should test a gated vs ungated whitepaper on the first send — A/B.
[09:00] Lena Park: Agree. We'll set up two landing pages.
[09:12] Ava Martinez: Perfect. Any other Qs?
[09:18] Omar Haddad: No — will follow up on venue specifics.
[09:22] Priya Singh: Thanks all.

Recap / Next steps:
- Ava to send run of show deck + sample emails + 2-sentence bios (due 2025-07-11)
- Derek to share demo checklist, fallback plan, and latency snapshot (due 2025-07-16)
- Omar to confirm AV specs and rooming (due 2025-07-14)
- Lena/Priya to build two landing pages for gated/ungated test (due 2025-07-15)
